rsguide: diagnosis of remote sensing data and suggestion of analyses

Source: R/rsguide-package.R
rsguide-package.Rd

rsguide takes remote sensing data, automatically identifies what they are and suggests which analyses are possible. Each suggestion comes with a plain-language rationale, the necessary caveats and an example code snippet already filled in with your files and bands. The package does not run the analyses: it diagnoses and recommends.

Workflow

  1. diagnose() takes the data (files, folders or R objects) and describes each one: type, layers, resolution, coordinate reference system, bands and sensor, value scale, DEM, time series and raster/vector overlap. It then calls suggest_analyses().

  2. print() shows the diagnosis, the alerts and the list of suggested analyses.

  3. summary() shows the rationale, caveats and packages of each analysis.

  4. show_code() prints the example code, ready to copy.

  5. as.data.frame() exports the report as a table.

Accepted inputs

  • Rasters: .tif, .tiff, .vrt, .img, .jp2, .nc, .grd, .asc files or SpatRaster objects (terra).

  • Vectors: .shp, .gpkg, .geojson, .json, .kml files or sf, sfc and SpatVector objects.

  • Tables with coordinates: .csv, .txt, .tsv files (separated by commas, semicolons or tabs) or data.frames. Recognized columns: lon/lat, long/lat, lng/lat, longitude/latitude, decimalLongitude/decimalLatitude (GBIF), x/y, easting/northing, utm_x/utm_y, among others.

  • Folders: every recognized file inside the folder.

  • Several inputs at once: diagnose(image, points).

Recognized sensors and bands

  • Sentinel-2: B1/B01 to B12, B8A, SCL, also inside file names such as ..._B04_10m.jp2.

  • Landsat 8/9 (Collection 2): SR_B1 to SR_B7, ST_B10, QA_PIXEL and the short names B1 to B11.

  • Landsat 4-7 (Collection 2): SR_B1 to SR_B5, SR_B7, ST_B6.

  • Generic names: blue, green, red, rededge, nir, swir1, swir2, thermal, the names used in STAC catalogs (nir08, swir16, swir22, ...) and their Portuguese equivalents (azul, verde, vermelho, ...).

The aliases are listed in system.file("rules", "bands.csv", package = "rsguide"). When the names match more than one sensor, the package warns you; set the sensor with diagnose(x, sensor = "landsat89").

Options

  • rsguide.min_multispectral_bands (default 4): minimum number of spectral bands for the data to be considered multispectral.

  • rsguide.min_dates_long_series (default 10): minimum number of dates to suggest trend analysis.

  • rsguide.sample_size (default 100000): number of cells read to estimate statistics of large rasters.

Learn more

  • vignette("case-study-jurua", package = "rsguide"): case study with Sentinel-2 images of the Jurua River (Acre, Brazil).

  • vignette("custom-rules", package = "rsguide"): how to add new analyses to the rules table.

  • rsguide_rules(): the rules table and the available tags.

  • jurua_data: the example data.
